bioghist.head: Bessie Emanuel
bioghist.p: Bessie Emanuel (1902-1984), later Bessie Emanuel Smith, was a teacher and activist. She was raised in White Plains, New York by her father Christopher H. Emanuel, a Baptist minister, and her mother Lucy Kittrell Emanuel. She attended an integrated high school, and then received an elementary education degree from Hampton Institute (now Hampton University) in 1925. Emanuel later received a master's degree in education at Columbia University. She had a long career in elementary education teaching at schools such as the New York City School for the Blind. She returned to White Plains in 1945 where she was the first Black teacher in the town's history. She served as vice president of the White Plains chapter of the NAACP and received the National Sojourner Truth Award, the highest honor offered by the National Association of Negro Business and Professional Women's Clubs.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Collections are processed to a variety of levels, depending on the work necessary to make them usable, their perceived research value, the availability of staff, competing priorities, and whether or not further accruals are expected. The library attempts to provide a basic level of preservation and access for all collections, and does more extensive processing of higher priority collections as time and resources permit.
These materials have been arranged and described according to national and local standards. For more information, please refer to the Beinecke Archival Description Unit Processing Manual.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This collection contains a mix of correspondence and ephemera from Bessie Emanuel's early life. The bulk of the materials relate to Emanuel's elementary and higher education at White Plains High School and Hampton Institute.

'Early school papers' contains notebooks, assignments and essays from elementary school and her diary captures daily activity from her junior year of high school. Correspondence with Jacob Smith, her eventual husband, were written while Smith was studying to be a teacher at Hampton Institute, the University of Iowa, and Shaw University in North Carolina. Other letters are from Philadelphia and Sayville, Long Island.
'General correspondence' and 'School and professional correspondence' contain letters to family and friends as well as communication about potential jobs and school updates.
'Hampton Institute printed ephemera' and 'Personal papers' focus on Emanuel's time at the Hampton Institute and beyond and include resumes, class schedules and records.
'March 2026 Acquisition' contains correspondence, photographs, and an autograph book from the early life of Bessie Emanuel.
